title: Moving against the odds with a cyclic active Brownian ratchet: current enhancement and reversal
authors: Theo Spornhauer, Benoît Mahault, Johannes Zierenberg
abstract: We show that periodically modulating the self-propulsion of active particles in an asymmetric potential can both enhance rectified transport and reverse its direction, even when the propulsion speed itself never changes sign. Current enhancement results from the nonlinear response of active transport to propulsion strength, whereas current reversal emerges from the interplay between activity-induced spreading and passive relaxation. Our theoretical analysis identifies the regimes governed by these distinct rectification mechanisms and predicts the finite range of driving periods over which current reversal occurs. These results establish cyclic activity as a means of dynamically controlling rectified active transport, with potential applications to the selective sorting of active particles.
summary: This paper theoretically analyzes active Brownian particles moving in an asymmetric potential under periodically modulated self-propulsion. It demonstrates that this cyclic activity can enhance the directed current beyond what is expected from simple averaging, and critically, it shows that the current can be reversed by tuning the driving period. This establishes cyclic activity as a powerful tool for dynamically controlling active transport.
main_problem: The study investigates how periodically modulating the self-propulsion of active particles in an asymmetric potential (active ratchet) affects the resulting directed transport.
main_result: Cyclic activity can significantly enhance the rectified transport current compared to non-cyclic driving, and it can even reverse the current direction under specific conditions.
method: The analysis combines theoretical derivations using Fokker-Planck equations and detailed approximations for mean displacement during active and passive phases.
model_or_system: The model consists of an Active Brownian Particle (cABP) moving in two dimensions within an external, asymmetric potential V(x), subjected to a time-dependent, cyclic self-propulsion speed v(t).
key_observables: Steady-state average current ($\langle \dot{x} \rangle$), enhancement factor ($\varepsilon$), and the conditions for current reversal.
important_parameters: Active fraction ($\alpha$), driving period ($T$), asymmetry parameter ($\lambda$), and the mean propulsion speed ($\langle v \rangle_T$).
main_assumptions: Approximations include neglecting rotational noise in some derivations and assuming constant self-propulsion speed during the active phase.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the particle trajectory, the ratchet potential, and phase diagrams mapping out the regimes of positive, zero, and negative current as a function of driving parameters.
paper_structure: The paper first analyzes the non-cyclic ratchet current using the Fokker-Planck equation, then develops an approximation scheme for cyclic driving, calculating mean displacements during active and passive phases to predict current enhancement and reversal.
why_interesting: The work provides a detailed, non-equilibrium statistical mechanics framework for controlling directed motion using time-periodic driving, which has parallels in understanding energy pumping or directed transport in complex active matter systems.
